clue.text: Plant finally rejected, say, but leading in 22 dn

indicators.note: finally places the turned-round piece at the end, after the Latin word

parts.note: in 22 dn, i.e. in Latin, the word for but is sed

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation for say is thrown back, read right to left

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A plant has been finally turned down, though it led the way in something Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: '22 dn' refers to the answer at 22 down, the language of ancient Rome, so 'but' is wanted in that language; 'leading' puts it first. 'rejected' is the reversal signal and 'finally' puts the reversed piece last.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedge is a grass-like marsh plant with solid triangular stems.

clue.text: A character familiar to underwriters

parts.note: reads as an insurance-world personality; really a small letter written below the line

explanation.surface: A well-known personality in the insurance trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Underwriters are insurers, but here also writers of things underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscript is a small character set below the normal line of type.

clue.text: Democrat unusually late in making a mark

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of late are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: A Democrat is unusually late to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' is the anagram signal for the four letters after the Democrat. 'in making' is only a link, leaving 'a mark' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter is used as a symbol for change, and a delta grade is a mark given in exams.

clue.text: In City University, record English poem

indicators.note: In means the record sits inside the city and university letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a log is a record

explanation.surface: At City University someone records an English poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, often a dialogue between shepherds.

clue.text: They pour cold water on expectations about mince-pies

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the expectations surround the minced letters

parts.note: expectations are hopes

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so the letters of the word pies are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dampens everyone's high hopes for the Christmas mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of the festive pies, but it is the anagram signal for the word after it; 'about' is the container signal. 'Pour cold water on' is meant literally, though it reads as the idiom for discouraging.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoses are literally used to spray water, so they pour cold water on things.

clue.text: Musical party affecting our overheads

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A musical party has an effect on our running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' looks like business costs but means what is on top of our heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A styled arrangement of hair sits on top of one's head.

clue.text: Bolted after supporters climbed up and stole

indicators.note: after places the bolted piece following the turned supporters
in a down clue climbed up means the supporters are written bottom to top

parts.note: fans are supporters
bolted means fled

explanation.surface: Someone escaped once fans had climbed up, and stole something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbed up' is the reversal signal, fitting a down clue, where reversed letters read upwards; 'after' says the bolted piece follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is to take something for oneself, to pinch it.

clue.text: Do surgeons use it on old boy involved in crash?

indicators.note: involved in means the old boy is wrapped inside the crash

parts.note: prang is British slang for a crash

explanation.surface: Would surgeons use this on a former pupil hurt in an accident?
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A probang is a slender rod for pushing obstructions down a patient's throat.

clue.text: Safe to pretend this is silk ribbon?

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to sham is to pretend

explanation.surface: Is it safe to pretend this is silk ribbon?
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a thick corded silk ribbon used for hatbands and belts.

clue.text: Hollow space used, in battles in Ushant.

indicators.note: used, in says the letters are used from within a run of the clue's words

explanation.surface: A hollow space used in sea battles off Ushant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ushant is an island off Brittany, scene of naval battles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a cavity, such as the air cavities in the skull bones.

clue.text: Welsh lake sounding similar to a Russian music-maker

parts.note: Bala Lake (Llyn Tegid) is the largest natural lake in Wales

indicators.note: sounding says the phrase is to be heard and its sound written down

parts.note: similar to a means like a

explanation.surface: A lake in Wales is said to resemble a Russian instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' is the homophone signal: 'like a' said aloud gives the second half. Bala Lake is in Gwynedd, north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The balalaika is a triangular, three-stringed Russian folk instrument.

clue.text: Frequently concerning X

parts.note: concerning means of, as in a tale of woe
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Something often has to do with the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequently and repeatedly happening means it happens many times.

clue.text: Our stand-in diplomat in Paris?

parts.note: reads as a British envoy deputising in France; really the French term for a deputy diplomat

explanation.surface: Britain's acting envoy in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a French phrase, so 'in Paris' gives the language it is in, not just where the diplomat is posted.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge d'affaires is a diplomat who stands in for an absent ambassador or heads a minor mission.

clue.text: Chemical compound not all found in a single river

indicators.note: found in means the partial quantity is set within the other letters

parts.note: a single means one, the Roman numeral I
not all means some

explanation.surface: A chemical that isn't present throughout is found in one particular river.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomers are compounds sharing a formula but with atoms arranged differently.

clue.text: Defeat Head of History in open argument

indicators.note: in means the initial letter sits inside the open argument

parts.note: overt means open
a row is an argument

indicators.note: Head of picks the first letter of History

explanation.surface: Defeating the head of history department in a public quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow is to topple or bring down, as with a government.

clue.text: Not a spineless type, Mrs Tiggywinkle

explanation.surface: Mrs Tiggy-winkle is no pushover.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Tiggy-winkle is the washerwoman in a Beatrix Potter children's book, and she is a hedgehog. 'Spineless' looks like weak-willed but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is covered in spines, and Beatrix Potter's laundress character is one of these creatures.

clue.text: He denies, for, example, interrupting a profiteer

indicators.note: interrupting means the example breaks into the profiteer

parts.note: a gainer is one who profits
say means for example

explanation.surface: A man denies, for instance, interrupting a profiteer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, so one who does it is a contradictor.

clue.text: Momentous event in history of two currencies?

definitions.text: Momentous event in history of two currencies?

parts.words: Momentous event in history of two currencies?
parts.note: a turning point, read whimsically as the pound sign joined by a conjunction to the old German currency

explanation.surface: A turning point in the history of two monies.
explanation.walkthrough: Two currencies, L (pound) and MARK, joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A milestone or turning point in history is a significant event.

clue.text: Divine ruler's article confused actor

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: confused means the letters of actor are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: An article about a god-like ruler mixed up an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' is the anagram signal for the word actor; the 's after 'Divine ruler' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A theocrat rules in the name of God, or as a god.

clue.text: Disastrous, romance for the Amatis here?

indicators.note: Disastrous suggests the letters of romance have been wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An ill-fated love affair for the Amati family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amatis were a family of violin makers in Cremona, Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is the Italian city where the Amati family made violins.

clue.text: Dish I prepare perfunctorily in the first place

indicators.note: in the first place puts the careless preparation before the letter I

parts.note: to scamp work is to do it hastily and carelessly

explanation.surface: A cook admits to a dish being slapdash from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the first place' sounds like 'originally' but means SCAMP goes first, ahead of I.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi is a seafood dish of breaded langoustine tails.

clue.text: The Commander's meat diet is antelope

indicators.note: diet says the commander takes in the meat, so it goes inside

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
ham is a meat
taken as written

explanation.surface: The commander lives on meat, which turns out to be antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamois is a goat-antelope of the European mountains.

clue.text: A key worker in the pool

definitions.text: A key worker in the pool

parts.words: A key worker in the pool
parts.note: reads as an essential worker at a swimming pool; really someone striking keys in a typing pool

explanation.surface: An essential employee at the swimming baths.
explanation.walkthrough: A typing pool was an office of shared secretaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist strikes keys and once worked in a typing pool.

clue.text: Sectarians in Utah, say, translated it incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly means the letters of the three words are set down wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Mormons in Utah supposedly translated something badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link offering an example but is part of the fodder; 'incorrectly' rearranges SAY TRANSLATED IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mormons formally call themselves the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, headquartered in Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Shakespeare's small tongue, according to Jonson?

definitions.text: Shakespeare's small tongue, according to Jonson?

parts.words: Shakespeare's small tongue, according to Jonson?
parts.note: Ben Jonson wrote that Shakespeare had small ... and less Greek

explanation.surface: Ben Jonson's verdict on Shakespeare's command of a language.
explanation.walkthrough: In his tribute poem, Jonson said Shakespeare had 'small Latine and lesse Greeke'.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical language of ancient Rome, which Jonson said Shakespeare knew only a little of.

clue.text: Ingenuous leader of intercessions in the body of the church

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the body of the church

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of intercessions

explanation.surface: A guileless person leads the prayers in the main part of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and lacking experience.

clue.text: Part of body discovered in centre of Tooting or thereabouts

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the seven-letter word Tooting

parts.note: or thereabouts means approximately, or so

explanation.surface: Body parts turned up somewhere near Tooting, in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: Tooting is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Girl in a place they finally found for fatness

indicators.note: in means the girl's name sits inside the other letters

parts.note: to posit is to place or put forward
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of they

explanation.surface: A girl turns up somewhere they eventually discovered was for weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adiposity is a state of being obese, from adipose tissue.

clue.text: Races here to secure a fresh sales outlet?

explanation.surface: Racing here might bring a new shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket in Suffolk is the home of British horse racing; a new market is a fresh outlet for sales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk town hosts major horse races, and split in two it describes a newly opened place to sell goods.

clue.text: Neat guide

explanation.surface: A tidy guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' here is the old word for cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for an ox or bullock, a young castrated male bovine; to direct a vehicle is to guide it.
